question: Which local tissue messengers help soften the cervix and start uterine contractions?
explanation: Prostaglandins E2 and F2 alpha are produced locally in reproductive tissues to help the cervix ripen and prepare the uterus for contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why are synthetic prostaglandins usually placed directly into the vagina or cervix instead of being swallowed as regular pills?

options.A: Pills take too long to dissolve in the stomach fluids of pregnant women
options.B: Oral tablets cause severe damage to the lining of the human stomach
options.C: They break down very quickly near where they are made in local tissues
options.D: Direct application prevents the liver from filtering out the active drug

explanation: Prostaglandins have a very short lifespan in the body, so placing them right at the target organ ensures they work effectively before they degrade. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h1)

question: What scoring system do midwives commonly use to check if a cervix is ready and favorable before inducing labor?
explanation: The Bishop score looks at dilation, effacement, station, consistency, and position to see if the cervix is ready for labor. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h2)

question: How do prostaglandins physically change a firm, unripe cervix to make it soft?

options.A: They stimulate the local production of heavy scar tissue to widen the canal
options.B: They cause the muscular walls of the cervix to contract tightly until it opens
options.C: They dry out the cervical tissues to make them brittle and easy to tear
options.D: They break down rigid collagen and increase water retention in the tissue

explanation: Prostaglandins break down tough collagen fibers and pull water into the tissue, which makes the cervix soft and ready for delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main goal of using prostaglandins when labor needs to be started artificially in the hospital?

options.A: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: To relieve severe labor pain without using regional anesthesia
options.C: To soften and prepare an unfavorable cervix for delivery
options.D: To completely stop all uterine activity during preterm labor

explanation: Prostaglandins are primarily used when the cervix is still firm and closed, helping to prepare it before active labor begins. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h3)

question: A woman at 41 weeks of pregnancy is admitted for induction with a Bishop score of three. What is the best first step?

options.A: Start an immediate high-dose oxytocin intravenous infusion
options.B: Perform an emergency primary cesarean section right away
options.C: Send the patient home to wait for spontaneous labor to start
options.D: Administer a cervical ripening agent like prostaglandin

explanation: A Bishop score of three is low and means the cervix is unfavorable. Using a ripening agent helps prepare the cervix before moving on to oxytocin. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which medication was originally made for stomach ulcers but is now widely used for cervical ripening?
explanation: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin medication that is affordable and holds up well in warm climates, making it popular for labor induction. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of a dinoprostone vaginal insert over misoprostol tablets during labor induction?

options.A: It costs significantly less money for patients in low-resource clinics
options.B: It never causes any side effects related to stomach upset or fever
options.C: It remains completely stable even in very hot tropical climates without refrigeration
options.D: It can be physically removed from the vagina if uterine overactivity occurs

explanation: The dinoprostone insert has a retrieval string attached, allowing a midwife to pull it out easily if the uterus starts contracting too frequently. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the standard recommended starting dose of misoprostol when placed in the vagina for cervical ripening?
explanation: Starting with a low dose of 25 micrograms helps prevent sudden, overly strong contractions and keeps the process safe. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why must midwives be very careful with standard commercial misoprostol tablets found in general hospital pharmacies?

options.A: Oral tablets will dissolve instantly upon contact with any vaginal moisture
options.B: The drug manufacturer strictly forbids its use by midwives in maternity wards
options.C: Tablets meant for ulcers contain doses that are far too high for safe labor induction
options.D: The medication loses all of its chemical potency within ten minutes of exposure to air

explanation: Stomach ulcer tablets usually come in 200-microgram doses, which are much too strong for induction and can cause dangerous complications if not properly divided. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h5)

question: What assessment should a midwife always perform right BEFORE giving a cervical ripening prostaglandin?

options.A: Administer a prophylactic dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Insert a large-bore intravenous line for rapid fluid loading
options.C: Confirm a reassuring fetal heart rate pattern
options.D: Perform an artificial rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Checking the baby's heart rate first ensures the baby is doing well before introducing a medicine that changes uterine activity. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why is fetal heart monitoring required for a period right after a prostaglandin insert is placed?

options.A: To measure the exact internal temperature of the amniotic fluid pocket
options.B: To prove to the hospital insurance company that the medication was given correctly
options.C: To speed up the physical softening of the maternal cervix through electrical waves
options.D: To catch sudden changes in fetal heart rate caused by unexpected uterine contractions

explanation: Close monitoring ensures that if the medication causes the uterus to contract too rapidly, the healthcare team can spot and address it quickly. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to avoid using prostaglandins for labor induction?

options.A: A previous classical uterine scar from past surgery
options.B: A history of a low-risk appendectomy in childhood
options.C: Known maternal allergy to prostaglandin medications
options.D: Complete placenta previa blocking the cervical os

explanation: Removing an appendix is a general abdominal surgery that does not affect the uterus, unlike a vertical uterine scar which carries a high risk of tearing. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why does a history of a previous vertical (classical) cesarean section mean prostaglandins should not be used?

options.A: The vertical upper uterine scar has a very high risk of tearing apart under strong contractions
options.B: The muscular wall becomes completely paralyzed and will never contract again
options.C: Prostaglandins interact dangerously with old scar tissue and cause permanent nerve damage
options.D: The previous surgical incision prevents the cervix from ever producing any collagen

explanation: Vertical scars in the upper part of the uterus are weak points that can easily rupture when powerful labor medications are introduced. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h7)

question: How is uterine tachysystole defined during labor induction monitoring?

options.A: Contractions lasting continuously for over fifteen minutes without a break
options.B: Fewer than two contractions in a full twenty-minute observation window
options.C: More than five contractions in ten minutes averaged over thirty minutes
options.D: Painful uterine cramping that occurs only once every hour during the night

explanation: Tachysystole means having too many contractions in a short time, which can lower blood flow to the placenta and stress the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)

question: A patient having labor induced with misoprostol develops six contractions in ten minutes, and the fetal monitor shows late decelerations. What is the midwife's first action?

options.A: Document the findings and wait another thirty minutes to see if it stops
options.B: Turn the patient to her left side and apply oxygen
options.C: Administer a dose of synthetic oxytocin to regularize the rhythm
options.D: Encourage the woman to push hard with the next contraction

explanation: Helping the mother lie on her side and giving oxygen improves blood flow to the placenta and helps relieve stress on the baby during too many contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)
